transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-06-21
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE); Priya Natarajan (Redwood SE); Maya Rivera (Novus - Head of ML); Tom Bennett (Novus - Platform Engineer); Asha Kapoor (Novus - CTO)

Summary (auto): quick discovery to understand Novus's ML infra, evaluate Redwood PLG quickstart (self-serve API, free credits), and surface security/VPC needs for a pilot.

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, im alex chen from Redwood, im an AE, with priya our se, hows everyone doing?
[00:10] Maya: good, thanks, excited to learn more, we looked at the docs, curious about quickstart and how fast we can get tokens flowing.
[00:18] Priya: great, we'll run through time-to-first-token, the trial credits, and then dig into your constraints — latency, data residency, and whether hosted is good enough or you need dedicated/private.
[00:30] Tom: quick heads up, our infra is on AWS in us-west-2, most services in a VPC and we have strict egress rules, so VPC peering or Private deployment is a big question.
[00:45] Alex: totally, makes sense. for the quickstart, you can sign up self-serve, we give free credits for a short trial, there's a sample curl and an npm/python sdk, time-to-first-token is often <5 minutes if you do the self-serve flow.
[00:58] Maya: <laugh> that's what we want, low friction. but for production we care about latency, we've got a realtime assistant feature, target p95 token latency ~120ms.
[01:15] Priya: okay, so realtime use means we should talk about model choice and hosting. our hosted API is the fastest for onboarding, but for predictable p95 you can go Dedicated with reserved capacity; private gives you VPC and on-prem options.
[01:30] Asha: what about data retention? we can't send certain logs externally.
[01:36] Alex: we have options — hosted by default doesn't store PII in logs, and we offer audit logs and optional customer-managed KMS for encryption. for stricter requirements, the Private deployment gives you a control plane in your VPC.
[01:52] Tom: can you do VPC peering for hosted? or is that only with Private?
[01:58] Priya: we do VPC peering for Dedicated and there are ways to do secure networking for hosted via private endpoints in some regions; full VPC control is typically Private. we'll share a network diagram.
[02:12] Maya: cool. also curious about cost — we prototyped with OpenAI and Anthropic; cost per token is a big driver for us.
[02:20] Alex: yes, cost is one of our levers — batching, KV caching, and quantized model variants can reduce token cost; Redwood Optimize suggests config. for pilot, we usually recommend default hosted with a smaller quantized open model to validate quality/cost.
[02:38] Tom: does Redwood provide any benchmarks? we want to compare latency/cost against our current endpoints on SageMaker.
[02:45] Priya: absolutely — we have internal perf profiles, and we can run a short benchmark for you using your sample workload; we'll need a representative prompt set and token length distribution.
[02:58] Asha: sso/saml and SOC 2 are also on our security checklist. are you SOC 2 certified?
[03:03] Alex: yes, Redwood is SOC 2 Type II. we'll share compliance pack and a red-team security doc. also can provide pen test reports under NDA.
[03:15] Maya: good. elaborating on the pilot, our success criteria are: p95 token latency <= 150ms for 512 tokens, cost per 1k tokens below current baseline, and no data exfiltration concerns.
[03:30] Priya: that's clear and achievable maybe with the right model and Dedicated if needed; for the quickstart pilot we can try hosted first to validate functional correctness and cost/latency on your workload, then iterate to Dedicated if p95 needs tightening.
[03:46] Tom: any gotchas for time-to-first-token? network auth?
[03:50] Alex: usually folks sign up, create an api key, hit the sample curl, and done; if you want to onboard engineers we'll invite you to a trial org and provide a sandbox endpoint. if you need VPC setup, that adds some networking steps.
[04:05] Maya: ok, can you walk through what the quickstart docs include?
[04:09] Priya: sure — quickstart has a signup link, sample curl/python/js, recommended models, and an eval harness to test latencies. we also include examples for streaming and function calling. time-to-first-token is documented in the quickstart.
[04:25] Alex: i'll paste the quickstart link in chat after the call (link: https://redwood.ai/quickstart) and invite you to the trial org.
[04:33] Maya: perfect.
[04:40] [05:00] Speaker 2: question — you mentioned quantization — does that change quality?
[05:06] Priya: yes, lower-bit quantization can slightly affect quality; we recommend 4-bit or 8-bit profiles and run a quick eval suite against your prompts. Redwood Optimize will flag regressions.
[05:20] Tom: for the pilot, we need a config template for the request/response sizes and concurrency. can you share that?
[05:26] Priya: yes, we'll share a benchmark plan template and the runner.
[05:30] [10:00] Maya: ok, on the security side, we have to ensure keys are rotated and logs are centrally stored in our SIEM. can we push logs to our S3?
[10:12] Alex: you can export audit logs and integrate with SIEM; for hosted we retain logs for X days, but for dedicated/private longer retention and direct S3 export is available as an add-on.
[10:25] Asha: what about encryption at rest with customer managed keys?
[10:29] Priya: customer-managed KMS is supported for Private and for Dedicated we can provide KMS integration; hosted has encryption but not always CMK by default — we can discuss.
[10:40] Tom: networking again — do you need us to open specific ports?
[10:43] Priya: usually outbound to our endpoints over TLS; for VPC peering/Dedicated we'll share the exact CIDR ranges and ports. we'll include that in the network diagram.
[10:55] Maya: also curious about model updates and rollouts — we don't want sudden regressions.
[11:00] Alex: Redwood Console provides rollout controls: canary, A/B, automatic fallback to previous version. we also integrate evals and regression alerts tied to prompt sets.
[11:14] Maya: nice. and can you host our fine-tuned model?
[11:18] Priya: yes, we can host customer models on Dedicated or Private; for hosted we support hosted fine-tuning on specific plans — we should scope that if you want custom weights.
[11:30] Tom: any limits on request throughput for the trial?
[11:33] Alex: trial has soft rate limits; for the benchmark we'll request temporary uplift to test desired concurrency.
[11:40] Asha: if we go Dedicated, what's the procurement lead time?
[11:44] Alex: Dedicated provisioning is typically a few weeks depending on region and GPU availability; contract lead time depends on procurement but onboarding for Private can be a month or two if on-prem.
[11:56] Maya: price signals matter — can you give a rough per-token delta vs OpenAI?
[12:02] Alex: depends a lot on model and quantization; for many open models on Redwood cost can be 30-60% lower than comparable hosted alternatives after quantization and caching. we'll put numbers in the pricing doc.
[12:18] [20:00] Tom: ok, sample workload — it is a user-assistant flow, average 350 tokens per response, often streaming; we need server-side streaming and low tail latency.
[20:12] Priya: streaming is supported; we'll share best practices for buffering and chunking. KV cache helps for repeated prefixes.
[20:26] Maya: are there any developer SDKs for node/python?
[20:29] Alex: yes, node/python/go SDKs, examples in the quickstart.
[20:35] [30:00] Priya: next steps from our side: we'll build a benchmark plan, spin up a quick hosted sandbox for you, and run your prompt set through a sample model. Alex will send pricing and trial invite.
[30:12] Alex: i'll also include the SOC2 pack, network diagram, and a template for the benchmark.
[30:20] Tom: for the benchmark we prefer to run it during your business off-peak to avoid noise.
[30:24] Priya: noted.
[30:30] Maya: any blockers on our side? we need to confirm who will provision S3/test data and who on our infra team will be the point person.
[30:36] Asha: i'll have Tom own infra, and maya will provide the example prompts.
[30:42] Alex: great. so to recap: Redwood to send quickstart + trial invite + pricing + security docs; Priya to share benchmark plan & config; Novus to provide sample prompt set and S3 access; schedule pilot kickoff next week.
[30:58] Maya: sounds good.
[31:05] [40:00] Speaker 3: quick question — competition, any concerns about vendor lock-in?
[40:08] Alex: good question — Redwood provides compatible APIs and you can pin model versions; for portability we support standard model formats and export tools.
[40:18] Tom: final ask: can you include an estimate for Dedicated vs hosted for our pilot scale (100 concurrent users, avg RPS ~25)?
[40:26] Alex: yes, we'll produce a ballpark in the pricing doc and include the assumptions.
[40:34] Asha: thanks everyone, appreciate it.
[40:38] Alex: thanks all, we'll follow up with docs and invite.
[40:42] Priya: thanks, bye.
